newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates ease in late trade, fx outflows.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates ease in late trade, fx outflows.

text.p: About 150 million ecus were bought at the central bank's fixing and ecu/drachma was hovering around 301.600 in late dealing with depos exhibiting softness and forex forwards easing in long tenors, traders said.

"Banks bought about 150 million ecus for drachmas at the fixing and ecu/drachma was trading around 301.600 in late uneventful trade," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Depos are softer and forex forwards are easier in longer periods."
Forex forwards in six month to 12 month periods had dipped about five basis points, the dealer said.
Other dealers said liquidity was enhanced by inflows for pension payments to take place later this month which more than offset forex outflows, putting downward pressure on depos and forex forwards.

"We see banks based abroad on the offer side of forwards which means they see interest rates declining further," he said. "Ecu purchases at the fixing have to do more with profit taking rather than anything else."
Bond dealers said there was some buying interest for FRNs due 2002 from abroad.
"There was some interest for FRNs due 2002 from abroad," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. "In my view, they are trying to gauge the local mood going into the elections."
Early elections will be held September 22 but the market has taken a positive attitude towards them on the ground that the winner will have no option but to follow Greece's EU convergence plan.

Polls show the two major parties, the conservatives and the socialists, running neck and neck. A recent informal Reuters poll showed that the markets thought Simitis would finally emerge as the winner.
The mark was quoted at 159.13/18 drachmas from Thursday's 159.170 fix, the dollar at 240.27/37 drachmas from 240.250 and the Ecu at 301.52/62 from 301.600 drachmas.
"I'm not worried about ecu outflows at the fixing," said a forex dealer. "The central bank guided ecu/drachma to a level that lured players to take profits given the interest rate differential."
